subject: EdgeFin: performance/SLO qualification + benchmark methodology follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@edgefin.com>, sre@edgefin.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: EdgeFin: performance/SLO qualification + benchmark methodology follow-up

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - great to meet the EdgeFin team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned before we run the benchmark:

Summary of requirements you shared
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (first-byte) target ~200ms for interactive workflows; per-token streaming p50/p95 targets you want us to measure separately.
- Throughput: baseline 100 requests/sec steady-state, with burst to 400 req/sec during market opens.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions expected; peak concurrency up to ~400 for short windows.
- Streaming: yes - incremental token streaming required (first-byte latency is critical) and clients will cancel mid-stream occasionally.
- Model/response size: median response length ~80 tokens, 95th ~400 tokens.

Proposed benchmark methodology (high-level)
1) Prompt set: we'll start with the prompt set you shared in the call; attached is our initial template (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv) - please confirm any PHI/sensitive examples need to be removed.
2) Warmup and run policy: 5 minute warmup per worker, 100 runs per prompt for steady-state.
3) Measurements: first-byte latency, per-token inter-arrival, p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and end-to-end; success rate (no stream drops) and error counts.
4) Concurrency tests: run with 50/100/200/400 concurrent sessions to produce latency curve.
5) Reproducibility: we'll publish the harness and seed config (attached: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.md) and produce raw logs + summarized CSVs.

Action items / ask from EdgeFin
- Confirm the final prompt set (or redactions) and share sample payloads (JSON/S3 link).
- Confirm which region you want the test run from (us-west/us-east/eu).
- Any egress rules or firewall/VPC constraints we should be aware of.

Proposed timeline
- Share redacted prompt set + sample payloads by Tue EOD (Jan 19).
- Redwood runs an internal verification run Wed; we propose a joint 30-45m benchmark session Thu morning PT.

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv, redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.md

Thanks - I can hop on a quick call to walk the team through the harness before the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@edgefin.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 13:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin: performance/SLO qualification + benchmark methodology follow-up

Thanks Marissa - good summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Latency: p95 ~200ms is correct for first-byte on short responses (<=80 tokens). For long generations we care more about per-token streaming cadence; please report per-token inter-arrival p50/p95.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 100 req/s steady; during market opens we may see bursts up to 400 req/s. The concurrency numbers above are per-region.
- Cold-starts: we have occasional cold-worker starts when we roll models; please include a short cold-start pulse measurement (10-15s window) to capture 95th effects.

We're attaching a small sample payloads bundle and a sanitized table of typical prompts (edgefin_sample_payloads.tar.gz). We'll upload the full production-like payloads to S3 by EOD Tue.

Security note: our security team will send the standard questionnaire; please confirm you can accept a short-term SSH-restricted access for the benchmark runner or if you prefer us to open sample endpoints.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: EdgeFin: performance/SLO qualification + benchmark methodology follow-up

Hi Jared - perfect, thanks for the clarifications and for the sample bundle. Confirming next steps and a slightly more detailed test plan so the SRE/security teams can vet:

Detailed benchmark plan (for SRE/security)- Harness: we'll run the Redwood benchmark harness in a customer-isolated test environment; the harness will stream tokens over a TLS connection and record per-token timestamps. The harness README lists all flags and seeds (see Drive doc link below).
- Warmup: 5 minutes per worker, with a short sequence of calibration requests to populate KV caches.
- Reproducibility: each experiment will include seed + run-id; logs and the harness config will be uploaded to the Drive folder.
- Measurements collected:
  * First-byte latency (ms) per request
  * Per-token inter-arrival times (ms)
  * p50/p95/p99 latency aggregations for first-byte and final-token
  * Success/error counts and cancellation rate (client-cancelled mid-stream)
  * CPU/GPU utilization and memory stats (we'll collect our agent metrics if you permit)
- Cold-start pulse: we'll schedule 3 short pulses during the run to capture tail effects from worker spin-ups.

Acceptance criteria (example)
- Steady-state at 100 req/s: first-byte p95 <= 200ms, error rate < 1%.
- Concurrency 200: p95 growth < 2x relative to baseline.

We can run the joint session Thu 21 Jan 2027 09:00 PT - does that work for you? We'll publish the harness and config to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEdgeFinBenchDoc and link the HubSpot deal EF-2027-0421.

Security/access: SSH-restricted access is ok for short-term bench agents; our infra team will coordinate a list of allowed IPs. If you prefer we can run from a public endpoint and you validate from your side - whichever is easier for you.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness_v1.md

Thanks,
Marissa
